result.summary: Prepared the direct check for the accepted conditional lease obligation, correlating each timeout’s prefix, completion, and lease result. Includes ordinary timeout as a control and preserves full-cluster reachability limitations.

selections.rationale: Register the initial partial map and preserve a concrete A2 contact-marker question. Code establishes heterogeneous marker qualification; documentation weakens a naive successful-acknowledgement interpretation. No obligation or Evidence is claimed. Next discriminator is applicability of higher-term response handling and whether independent replication or incoming RPC processing necessarily closes the suspected window.

Continue the same principal contact-marker lifecycle. The heartbeat-rejection variant has no acquired immediate-role-loss requirement; pipeline timeout is a stronger discriminator because it can create a fresh marker without a delivered reply, and the response interface explicitly limits validity to successful completion. Register this newly read dependency before constructing a local executed comparison. Do not infer a lease failure solely from the interface mismatch.

feedback.answered: The contact-only contract does not demand successful heartbeat acceptance. Newly read producer code also shows that pipeline readiness does not imply response success: timeouts publish futures, while the existing consumer reads response fields directly. Ordinary periodic replication is an alternate step-down route, not a proven finite bound under arbitrary delays.
remaining: Requirement gap narrowed: AppendFuture.Response explicitly requires Error completion and success; the lease contract concerns actual contact, but an API mismatch alone is not a completed authority-loss finding.
Local execution gap: run a real in-memory pipeline timeout, correlate its request/future identity, observe Error and marker before/after actual pipelineDecode consumption.
Initial-prefix and same-history gaps: full cluster election, pipeline activation and isolated no-contact interval have not been executed. Remote processing without reply remains possible.

target_profile.rationale: Adds the in-memory pipeline timeout variant and its actual source dependencies within the existing package and contact-marker boundary. selections.rationale: Next discriminator replaces the assumed failed-future producer with real InmemTransport pipeline execution. Each isolated scenario constructs a Leader state with expired contact and two Voters; it does not use BootstrapCluster/NewRaft or claim a legal election prefix. Receiver transport admits the request but no receiver Raft or reply producer runs, so no reply can be delivered. Pipeline future Error is awaited independently before real pipelineDecode reads the queued future. Ordinary replicateTo is the comparison path. Main loop, heartbeat, snapshot and verification workers are omitted to isolate the local writer/consumer effect; their absence prevents inference of cluster role duration. Raw marker times, completion/error, stable operation label and request identity are observed before a manual lease invocation. No application consequence, normative violation or property Evidence is claimed. Exploration finishes on actual future/decoder completion with bounded tool timeouts, not on a desired state.

scope.description: Local timeout-to-contact-to-lease comparison under explicitly constructed local state, using actual in-memory transport completion and actual Raft consumers.
assumptions: Exactly two Voters, local node and one remote peer; no membership change.
Node initially has local Leader state and a peer-contact marker older than LeaderLeaseTimeout; this is an assumed local prefix, not a claimed elected state.
No receiver Raft processes the queued request and no reply is sent; no other writer changes contact.
Lease check runs after the tested timeout consumer completes; omitted background workers isolate this conditional effect.
excluded: Proof of a legal election/startup history
Automatic lease scheduling or total role-retention duration
Application stale reads, client success, or incorrect log commitment
